sources.title: Bills of materials and formulas
sources.scope: BOM lines, approval versus activation, and date/site/quantity-constrained versions.
supported_claims: BOM version validity can depend on date, site, and quantity.
Approval and activation are distinct; activation identifies a default rather than every usable alternative.
Item, Phantom, Pegged supply, and Vendor lines have different effects.
sources.limitations: Already fetched in the approved manufacturing research catalog on the accessed date. This is conceptual ERP documentation, not evidence of live access. Unique-default rejection, exact decimal arithmetic, thresholds, and office-only allocation are sample policies, not a reproduction of the ERP engine.

sources.title: Phantom items
sources.scope: Expanding multilevel engineering groupings into material components.
supported_claims: Phantom structures can flatten multilevel groupings into manufacturing components.
Phantom processing is different from consuming the phantom grouping as an ordinary material item.
sources.limitations: Already fetched in the approved research catalog. No route merging, capacity planning, production estimation, or physical kitting is implemented. Eight levels, 5000 expanded line paths, leaf-only scrap, and once-per-component ceiling are explicit synthetic policies.

sources.title: Inventory blocking
sources.scope: Distinguishing physical stock, reserved quantities, and blocked inventory.
supported_claims: Blocking can prevent inventory from being processed or consumed.
Overlapping blocking records must not be added as separate physical inventory.
sources.limitations: Already fetched in the approved research catalog. Inputs are one normalized row per physical stock source, not a sum of ERP blocking transactions. Status, expiry, reservation, and inbound eligibility rules here are conservative sample policies. No inventory operation is performed.
